claims.text: The quinary alloy and compared quaternary and ternary subsets have fully recrystallized, single-phase FCC microstructures after identical thermomechanical processing.
The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy has a larger spread in constituent atomic sizes than its equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets.
The larger atomic-size spread in the quinary alloy causes greater local lattice-strain heterogeneity.
Heterogeneous local strain fields impede mobile dislocations.
Greater resistance to dislocation motion increases strain hardening.
Increased work hardening delays necking or strain localization.
The quaternary and ternary alloys have narrower atomic-size distributions than the quinary alloy.
Narrower atomic-size distributions produce more uniform lattice strains and lower resistance to dislocation motion.
Relative to the quinary alloy, the quaternary and ternary alloys will have lower variance in local lattice strain.
Relative to the quinary alloy, the quaternary and ternary alloys will have more spatially uniform dislocation-density distributions.
The quinary alloy will have a higher strain-hardening rate than the compared quaternary and ternary alloys.
The quinary alloy will exhibit delayed strain localization relative to the quaternary and ternary alloys.
Digital image correlation during tensile testing can measure local strain evolution.
The proposed combination of high-resolution synchrotron diffraction and DIC can provide full-field lattice-strain maps.
Microbeam Laue diffraction and in-situ TEM can quantify local dislocation densities together with lattice distortions in these alloys.
The comparison is restricted to room-temperature uniaxial tensile deformation of identically processed single-phase FCC specimens at controlled rates.
Grain-boundary character and minor compositional fluctuations could confound the proposed relationship.
Quantifying dislocation interactions in high-entropy alloys is challenging.

The hypothesis is falsified if the quinary alloy lacks statistically greater lattice-strain and dislocation-density heterogeneity than the subsets, or if its strain-hardening rate does not exceed theirs.
